conceptual assets.reasoning: The design declares a 32-bit signal lock_q that the generate/process block initializes and updates: `if (rstn_i = '0') then lock_q(i) <= '0'; elsif rising_edge(clk_i) then if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') then lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw; end if; end if;`. The bus_response process reads that storage into the response data (`bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel` or `bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q`). These RTL relations show lock_q is the module's authoritative stored spinlock state; corrupting its bits would violate the implemented update/read semantics, establishing an Integrity objective.

The concurrent assignment implements the index decode: `sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(i, 5))) else '0';`. sel(i) is used both in the write condition that updates lock_q and in read masking (`bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel`). The RTL therefore computes which lock bit(s) a request addresses; incorrect sel values would cause wrong bits to be accessed or returned, establishing Integrity.
